# Dōbutsu no Mori e+ PC/Android port v1.4.7

Version 1.4.7 of the port that runs [afe-decomp](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-decomp) (the どうぶつの森 e+ decompilation) on PC and Android.

## Changes since v1.4.6

A full check of the 64-bit builds (Android, 64-bit Windows and Linux), after the gyroid crash fixed in v1.4.6. What
it found and fixed:

- **Sound effects that replace each other as on the GameCube** (every PC and Android build).
  - **The problem:** when all six sound-effect slots are busy, a new sound replaces one with a lower priority. For
    some sound effects the game reads that priority from past the end of its table. On the GameCube that is the
    next table in memory; the PC builds read whatever their compiler had put there (on Linux, a piece of text),
    so these sounds replaced others, or were replaced, differently than on the GameCube.
  - **The fix:** the PC builds carry the GameCube's bytes after the table.
- **Sound state after an ambient sound fades** (Windows and Linux, most of all 64-bit Windows).
  - **The problem:** when a looping ambient sound finishes fading in or out, the game writes past the end of a
    small table into the next ones, and when a river sounds near a waterfall it reads past another. On the
    GameCube and on Android those tables sit one after another. The Linux builds leave gaps between them, so the
    writes changed other fields than on the GameCube; the 64-bit Windows build puts other variables there, so
    the writes reset an entry of the ambient-sound stack and the counter that stretches the vowels of the
    villagers' voices.
  - **The fix:** the tables are kept together in the GameCube's order, and the bytes written are the ones the
    GameCube writes.
- **Smaller fixes**, none of which showed on screen: a graphics function read 4 bytes past a command, two audio
  functions could cut a pointer to 32 bits or read past a table, a memory statistic was written through a pointer
  of the wrong size, and saving a photo to the SD card read past a small buffer (the photo is the same).
- Signed with the same key as the previous version, so it installs over it (saves, the Korean patch and texture
  packs are kept).

## Updating

- **From v1.0.0 or later**, the game finds this version when it starts and offers to update (**Update now**; on
  Android, **업데이트** in the dialog). If GitHub answers with an error, try again a little later.
- v0.1.6 and earlier cannot update themselves: install this version by hand once.
- The multiplayer protocol is the same as v1.4.x's: v1.4.0 to v1.4.7 can be in the same room, and 32-bit and
  64-bit players can play together.

## Read this first

- **No game data is included.** You need your own disc image of the Japanese 「どうぶつの森 e+」 **Rev 1 (GAEJ01)**
  (`.iso` / `.ciso` / `.gcm`) to run it. Disc images are not distributed.
- **To play in Korean**, download the Korean patch from [retrodb 한글패치 — 동물의 숲 e+](https://retrodb.info/krpatch/7428/%EB%8F%99%EB%AC%BC%EC%9D%98-%EC%88%B2-e)
  and apply it in the game (pause menu → Settings → Disc → Korean patch → Install...). The Korean patch is the work of an
  independent author (역전맞고) unrelated to this repository.
- Multiplayer: [README](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/blob/main/README.md#multiplayer). For players from
  other networks, the surest way is UPnP turned on in the host's router, or UDP 47070 forwarded to the host's device.

## Files

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.7-Windows-x64.zip` | 64-bit Windows. Includes `SDL2.dll`, requires OpenGL 3.3 |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.7-Windows-x86.zip` | 32-bit Windows (also runs on 64-bit Windows). Includes `SDL2.dll`, requires OpenGL 3.3 |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.7-Linux-x86_64.zip` | 64-bit Linux. Requires SDL2 (`libsdl2-2.0-0`) and an OpenGL 3.3 driver |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.7-Android.apk` | Android 5.0 or later, 32/64-bit ARM (armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | SHA-256 of the files above |

## Verified

- The same scripted play on a 32-bit and a 64-bit build, comparing every screenshot pixel for pixel, the logged
  positions and the saves:
  - built with gcc (the compiler of the Windows and Linux builds): 35 scenarios (the opening, building interiors,
    the whole part-time job, several days with letters, K.K. Slider and events, the Famicom, the Korean text
    editor, the device menus), 815 screenshots: all identical, and so are the saves;
  - built with clang (the compiler of the Android build): 14 scenarios, 491 screenshots: all identical.
- A 64-bit build with AddressSanitizer and UBSan bounds checks through all of these, every sound, and a walk through
  all 30 blocks of a later town by day and by night: no memory errors are left. The out-of-range reads that remain
  are in the original game's code and work the same way on every build (listed in the docs).
- Sound: every sound effect, BGM and gyroid melody, played one after another, sounds the same on 32-bit and 64-bit,
  sample for sample. The walk through the town sounds the same on 32-bit Linux, 64-bit Linux and 64-bit Windows
  (64-bit Windows sounded different from the first ambient fade before this version).
- The 키다리팀바 gyroid on 64-bit Windows (Wine): it is placed and the screens are the same as on Linux.
- All unit tests pass. The decomp changes are inside `TARGET_PC` only and the matching build's hashes are unchanged.
- Android: the release-key signature (certificate `db6fc1ad…`) and the version (1.4.7, versionCode 10407).

Details: [docs/64bit.md](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/blob/main/docs/64bit.md#audit-v147).

## Known limitations

- On the first day, nothing can be saved before you have met a villager: the game itself does not allow it.
- No test on a real arm64 device was possible here; arm64 runs the same 64-bit code that was checked on x86_64.
- The limitations of v1.4.3 remain (see its [release notes](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/releases/tag/v1.4.3)).

Build instructions and detailed progress are in [docs/README.md](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/blob/main/docs/README.md).
